basic.title: First Game Flow: Read, Prepare, Resolve
basic.description: Start with the win condition, mage readouts, channeling, and planning, then continue through summoning, public discard, the quickcast window, and movement.

steps.intro: Mage Wars lasts several rounds, until one mage has taken enough damage to be destroyed. The last mage standing wins the game.
steps.selfHud: Your mage panel shows life, damage, mana, channeling, action marker, and quickcast marker. Apprentice mages start with Life 24, Mana 10, and Channeling 10; your goal is to deal enough damage to defeat the opposing mage.
steps.opponentHud: The opponent panel shows the same readouts. Opponent prepared spells use card backs and a count, so card names stay hidden until revealed.
steps.stage: Each game round has two stages: the Ready Stage and the Action Stage. The Action Stage begins after the Ready Stage is complete.
steps.channelResult: The Beastmaster currently has Channeling 10; after channeling, the mana supply gains 10 mana.
steps.preparePlanning: Upkeep is resolving before planning begins.
steps.spellCardReading: Use this spell-card legend first: cost, action, range, target, type, school, and level determine how you prepare and cast.
steps.attackBarReading: Jungle Wolf is now in the arena. This is only a reading step, not a selection: the left icons tell quick or full action and melee or ranged attack; the right side shows range, damage type, attack dice, extra effects, and traits. Click Next when done.
steps.planCreatureNextPage: Click the next page to find Jungle Wolf.
steps.planSelectWolf: Jungle Wolf is a Creature spell: it summons a creature into the arena to keep fighting. Click the Jungle Wolf card body to put it into the first prepared slot.
steps.planIncantationNextPage: Click the next page to find Rouse the Beast.
steps.planSelectRouse: Rouse the Beast is an Incantation spell: it resolves a one-time text effect, then goes to your discard pile. Click the Rouse the Beast card body to put it into the second prepared slot.
steps.planConfirm: Click “Confirm prep 2/2” to submit this round's plan.
steps.prepareOpponentSpells: The opponent prepares spells through the formal flow; they stay card backs until revealed.
steps.preparedAndHidden: Both players choose their own spells at the same time. Your chosen spells are kept hidden from the opponent so they cannot know your plan.
steps.deploySelectWolf: Click Jungle Wolf in your prepared spells.
steps.wolfSummoned: Jungle Wolf has been summoned into the Beastmaster's zone. It enters without a ready action, so the spent action marker means it cannot act yet. This is a reading step: do not click the wolf yet, click Next to continue.
steps.rouseSelectSpell: Click Rouse the Beast in your prepared spells.
steps.rouseTargetWolf: Click the Jungle Wolf card body in the arena so Rouse the Beast targets it.
steps.passYourDeployment: Jungle Wolf's action marker is now ready. Click “End deployment”.
steps.opponentDeploymentResults: The opponent's deployment and one public attack spell are resolving through the formal flow.
steps.opponentPublicView: The opponent has resolved deployment and one public attack spell. Click the eye in the opponent panel's upper-left corner to switch to the opponent public view; this only reads public information and does not let you act for the opponent.
steps.discardReading: The same discard area now shows the opponent's public discard: resolved opponent spells stay here face up. Unrevealed prepared spells still remain card backs.
steps.backToSelfView: After reading the opponent's discard, click “Back to your view” to return to your spellbook, prepared spells, and next action.
steps.opponentPassDeployment: After the opponent finishes deployment, both players enter the initiative quickcast window. Quickcast is a rule timing window, not a response and not always-on free casting; now you decide whether to use a quick spell.
steps.skipInitiativeQuickcast: This is your initiative quickcast window. Quickcast is only available when the rules open this window; you are not casting now, so click “Pass quickcast”.
steps.opponentPassInitiativeQuickcast: The opponent also passes initiative quickcast, so your creature action begins. Next, use Jungle Wolf to move.
steps.moveSelectWolf: Click the Jungle Wolf card body in the arena to choose it as the moving creature.
steps.moveTargetZone: Click an adjacent zone to move.
steps.finish: You have now read the board and spell cards, channeled, prepared spells, summoned Jungle Wolf, read its attack bar, roused it, checked public discard, passed the quickcast window, and moved a creature. The basic tutorial is complete.
